axes.guide: hidden assumptions about the execution environment or inputs (perfect sandbox, pre-installed dependencies, available test suites, clean issue descriptions)
fairness of the comparison with baselines (same LLM, same token/cost budget, same number of attempts, numbers copied from other papers instead of re-run)
reliability of the benchmark data (contamination / leakage into LLM training data, small or self-constructed datasets, noisy or filtered subsets, LLM-as-judge metrics)
whether results transfer beyond the evaluated setting (only Python, few repositories, toy tasks instead of real codebases, single benchmark)
whether results can be reproduced (closed models that change, seeds, number of runs, variance, released code/configs, cost to reproduce)
